title: Identifying level-$k$ reasoning in repeated games: Strategies, beliefs, and cognitive ability
abstract: arXiv:2610.33098v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: In this paper, we identify level-$k$ reasoning in repeated games that operates at the level of a supergame strategy. First, we develop a model of level-$k$ reasoning that incorporates choices over strategies as well as beliefs about the strategies chosen by others. Then, jointly using elicited strategies and beliefs about strategies from the indefinitely repeated Prisoner's Dilemma, and applying a new notion of balance-optimal error tolerance, we classify a substantial fraction of subjects as level-1 or level-2. Moreover, we show that when level-$k$ reasoning operates at the level of a repeated-game strategy, cognitive ability and experience predict higher level reasoning.

translated_title: 在重复博弈中识别level-k推理：策略、信念与认知能力
translated_abstract: 本文在重复博弈中识别了在超级博弈策略层面运作的level-k推理。首先，我们开发了一个level-k推理模型，该模型同时纳入了对策略的选择以及对他人所选策略的信念。然后，通过联合使用从无限重复囚徒困境实验中引导出的策略及关于策略的信念，并应用一种新的“平衡最优容错”概念，我们将相当大比例的受试者分类为level-1或level-2。此外，我们表明，当level-k推理在重复博弈策略层面运作时，认知能力和经验可以预测更高层次的推理。
tldr: 本文在超级博弈策略层面识别level-k推理，开发了一个同时纳入策略选择与信念的模型，借助无限重复囚徒困境实验和新的平衡最优容错概念，将相当比例的受试者分类为level-1或level-2，并发现认知能力与经验能够预测更高层次的推理。
en_tdlr: This paper identifies level-k reasoning at the supergame strategy level in repeated games, develops a model incorporating both strategy choices and beliefs, classifies a substantial fraction of subjects as level-1 or level-2 using elicited strategies and beliefs from an indefinitely repeated Prisoner's Dilemma with a new notion of balance-optimal error tolerance, and shows that cognitive ability and experience predict higher-level reasoning.
